Long-press a word in any app (Chrome, WhatsApp, Kindle, Reddit…). With instant pop-up on, a panel slides up with a dictionary definition, a Wikipedia summary and a translation, without leaving the app you\'re in.\n\nSome apps don\'t report text selections to Android. There, pick \"Word Peek\" from the selection menu instead (you may need to tap ⋮ to see it).
Shows definitions as soon as you select a word

Word Peek watches for text you select in other apps. When you select a word or short phrase (up to 6 words), it shows its definition, Wikipedia summary and translation in a panel at the bottom of the screen.\n\nThe selected text is sent to dictionaryapi.dev, Wikipedia and MyMemory to look it up. Word Peek doesn\'t read or store anything else, and ignores password fields.
On. Long-press a word in any app to see its definition.
Off. Turn it on to see definitions as soon as you select a word, without opening the selection menu.
If Android says the setting is restricted (common for apps installed from a file): open App info below, tap ⋮ at the top right, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.
